TC-APT-042.title: Complex/idiomatic sentence structures produce recurring cross-language defects (parallel-negation-lists, verbed-noun idioms like 'round-trip', product-name+generic-noun link text)
TC-APT-042.blocking_reason: Originally opened for cells-spreadsheet-management-go's parallel-negation-list/nested-conditional-before-link sentences. CONCLUSIVE evidence added from introducing-words-foss-net's full 8-language review (ar,cs,de,el,es,fa,fr,he -- ALL 8 rejected even after both real pipeline bugs TC-APT-041/049 were fixed and confirmed working in every one). Two recurring defects, both narrowly scoped to 1-2 specific sentences on this page: (1) round-trip verbed-idiom sentence mistranslated in 5/8 (de,cs,el,fa,he), fine in 2/8 (es,fr) -- genuine per-language model variance, no clear pipeline explanation found. (2) '[Aspose.Words FOSS for .NET repository]' link text scrambled in 6/8 (ar,cs,es,fa,fr,he), borderline in el, unclear in de -- this one has a PLAUSIBLE architectural explanation, not just model variance: `_extract_link` (text_unit_extractor.py) always extracts link text as its own isolated TextUnit (kind=LINK_TEXT), translated WITHOUT the surrounding sentence's context ('The full source is available on GitHub in the [...]'). Translating a bare product-name+generic-noun compound with no sentence context to signal the required case/preposition is inherently harder than translating it in full-sentence context -- plausibly related to TC-APT-036's underlying concern (link content losing full-sentence coherence), though TC-APT-036 is specifically about LEAF-fallback paragraph fragmentation, not link-text isolation, so this may need its own investigation: does LINK_TEXT translation ever receive surrounding-sentence context, and would passing it help. NOT attempted this session -- context-passing to link-text translation is an architecture-level change, same weight class as TC-APT-041/049, deserves its own dedicated iteration with proper regression tests, not a rushed attempt at the tail of an already-long session. Gate 5 pivoted off this page (see TC-APT-014) rather than continuing to spend review budget on already-conclusive 8/8 evidence.

TC-APT-041.title: Commit a shard batch its passing jobs even when some jobs failed (stop losing partial progress to abort-on-first-failure)
TC-APT-041.blocking_reason: Implemented per peer session (hugo-translator-db) escalation to prioritize this over further Gate-5 page investigation. _run_locked() no longer raises per-shard on shard_failed -- it accumulates failed_shard_ids and lets the existing unconditional commit call + outer loop proceed to every remaining shard; commit is already safely scoped to checksum-receipted paths only. The run still ends non-zero when any job failed, but the raised CampaignManifestError now carries .summary (including failed_shard_ids) so callers see the full picture instead of a bare traceback -- run_gate4_canary.py/run_gate5_batch.py updated to print it. Also fixed the stray hardcoded `Co-authored-by: Codex <noreply@openai.com>` trailer, replaced with the runbook's actual content-repo convention (Claude Fable 5.1). New regression test (test_shard_failure_does_not_block_later_shard_commits) proves a failed first shard no longer blocks a later shard's commit; one existing test's stale abort-on-first-failure assertion updated to match. tests/unit/workers/ -> 543 passed, 1 skipped.
